full_judgment:
2. Facts in short are that the petitioner who is the judgment-debtor of Decree Execution Case No.2 of 2011 submitted a petition before the Executing Court under Order 21 Rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the proceedings of above execution case till disposal of Other Class Suit No.89 of 2020 filed by the petitioner as plaintiff challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree and passed on 2-3-2011 in SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 which was under execution in above case. 

 3. It was alleged that after passing of above judgment and decree in SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 against the petitioner who was the defendant in above suit by the Small Causes Court the petitioner as plaintiff has filed Title Suit No.89 of 2020 for a decree declaring that above judgment and decree of the Small Causes Court is unlawful and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. It was further stated that for the disputed premises the opposite party has further filed Suit No.160 of 2010 for partition and Land Survey Tribunal Suit No.5671 of 2014 against erroneous record of the disputed premise in the names of the opposite party. As such execution of above decree should be stayed till disposal of above three suits filed by the petitioner. 

 8. Mr Kamal Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 for eviction of the defendant-petitioner who was the tenant of the disputed premises and above suit was decreed on contest on 2-3-2011. Being aggrieved by above judgment and decree of the Small Causes Court the petitioner preferred Civil Revision No.1873 of 2011 to the High Court Division but the Rule was discharged on 29-9-2014. Challenging the legality and propriety of above judgment and order of the High Court Division the petitioner preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.3050 of 2014 to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh which was rejected on 8-5-2017. Thereafter challenging the legality and propriety of above judgment and decree dated 2-3-2011 passed in SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 the petitioner has filed Title Suit No.89 of 2020 and the same is pending for trial. The petitioner has also filed a suit for partition being Partition Suit No.160 of 2010 and Land Survey Tribunal Suit No.5671 of 2014 in the Land Survey Tribunal which are also pending for trial. As such the petitioner filed above petition for stay of the proceedings of SCC Execution Case No.2 of 2011. But the learned the learned Judge of the Small Causes Court has most illegally rejected above petition and the learned District Judge without an independent assessment of the materials on record most illegally dismissed the Civil Revision and affirmed above flawed judgment and order of the Execution Court which is not tenable in law. 

 9. On the other hand Mr Md Mahabubur Rashid, learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos.1 and 3-7 submits that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 for eviction of the petitioner who was a tenant of the opposite parties from the disputed premises and the suit was decreed on contest on 2-3-2011. Above judgment and decree was affirmed by the Appellate Division by rejection of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal filed by the petitioner. Opposite parties filed SCC Execution Case No.2 of 2011 for executing above decree of SCC Suit No.15 of 1998. But the petitioner has filed Title Suit No.89 of 2020 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge challenging the judgment and decree of the SSC Suit No.15 of 1998 which was decreed against him on contest and which was finally affirmed by the Appellate Division in the judgment and order passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No, 3050 of 2014 which is unlawful and not tenable in law. 

 11. It is admitted that the opposite party Nos.1-7 as plaintiffs filed SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 for eviction of the petitioner who was the sole defendant claiming that he was a defaulter tenant of the disputed premise and above suit was decreed on contest on 2-3-2011 and the petitioner preferred Civil Revision No.1873 of 2011 to the High Court Division challenging the legality and propriety of above judgment and decree of SCC Suit No.15 of 1998 which was rejected vide judgment and order dated 29-9- 2014. 

 13. As such the judgment and decree passed by the SCC Court in S No.15 of 1998 was merged in the judgment and order of Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.3050 of 2014. 

 15. The proceedings of Small Causes Court is a special and summary proceedings for expeditious disposal of small civil disputes and no appeal lies from the judgment and decree passed by a Small Causes Court. 

 16. Petitioner who was the sole defendant of SSC Suit No.15 of 1998 and he contested above suit. The petitioner challenged the legality and propriety of the above judgment and decree of SCC Suit No.151 of 1998 both to the High Court Division and to the Appellate Division by preferring Civil Revision No.1873 of 2011 and CPLA No.3050 of 2014 but of no avail. The Appellate Division has finally determined that the petitioner is a defaulter tenant of the disputed premises under the opposite parties. 

 18. The judgment and decree of a suit of the Small Causes Court cannot be challenged in a Civil Court by a party who participated in the above SSC proceedings. 

 22. The learned Senior Assistant Judge is directed to conclude the proceedings of Decree Execution Case No.2 of 2011 within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this order without any fail.
